title: Low-Pass Filter - Band 7 (2600 MHz) for IoT Narrowband Module
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Elena Vasquez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Low-Pass Filter filter targeting Band 7 (2600 MHz) for IoT Narrowband Module. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 4225.5 MHz and bandwidth of 199.0 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the IoT Narrowband Module module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Low-Pass Filter
- Frequency Band: Band 7 (2600 MHz)
- Application: IoT Narrowband Module
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)
- Design Tool: Sonnet EM Suite v16
- Design Center: Newbury Park Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Low-Pass Filter design targeting Band 7 (2600 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       4225.5 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       199.0 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 1.9 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 21.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 51.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 16.0 dB
Q Factor:               6933
Temperature Coefficient:-7.4 ppm/°C
Die Size:               3.0 x 2.0 mm
Wafer Size:             8-inch
Number of Resonators:   9
Electrode Material:     Mo/Al
Passivation:            SiO2/Si3N4 stack
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Sonnet EM Suite v16 and load the Low-Pass Filter template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 4225.5 MHz, BW 199.0 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 1.9 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (QFN (Quad Flat No-Lead)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (8-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Rohde & Schwarz ZNB40.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 12676 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 1.9 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 21.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 298 MHz offset >= 51.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 4 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 3.9 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +32 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 87%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-01-08
Devices Tested:         100
Insertion Loss (meas):  1.65 dB
Return Loss (meas):     22.6 dB
Rejection (meas):       53.6 dB
Isolation (meas):       20.8 dB
Q Factor (meas):        6933
Group Delay Variation:  2.0 ns
Power Handling:         +30 dBm
Die Yield:              89.7%

Result Classification:  NEEDS REVIEW
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Low-Pass Filter design demonstrated below-target performance for Band 7 (2600 MHz).
b) Insertion loss met target specification.
c) Out-of-band rejection exceeded the minimum requirement.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) Batch-to-batch reproducibility confirmed over 3 wafer lots.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
